title: Internal Workflow Dependency Map
purpose: Show how the 31 internal workflows connect to each other and to external boundaries — which workflows call which others, which share retry logic, which are fire-and-forget vs synchronous vs Socket.IO driven.
audience: Engineers debugging workflow interactions, architects planning background job migration
description: Comprehensive dependency map of all 31 internal workflows across 6 functional categories (Content, Payment, Messaging, Auth, Analytics, Admin). Each connection is labeled by triggering mechanism: synchronous calls (solid arrow), fire-and-forget with .catch() (dashed arrow), Socket.IO event emission (dashed with Socket label). Highlights that only 1 of 31 workflows (R2 Upload) has retry logic, that no queue/broker exists (all workflows execute synchronously or as unawaited promises), and that subscriber notification delivery is fire-and-forget with silent failure.

entryPoints.label: User Action / API Request
entryPoints.description: Most workflows are triggered by HTTP API requests from the frontend.

entryPoints.label: System Event (publish, report)
entryPoints.description: Some workflows are triggered by internal system events (content published, content reported).

entryPoints.label: Scheduled / Cron (none exist)
entryPoints.description: No scheduled jobs exist. Scheduled content publish triggers via the synchronous request path on page load.

exitPoints.label: Database Write
exitPoints.description: Workflow culminates in a database write (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

exitPoints.label: External API Call
exitPoints.description: Workflow calls an external service (R2, Ethereum RPC, Socket.IO, SMTP).

exitPoints.label: Fire-and-Forget
exitPoints.description: Workflow runs asynchronously with .catch()—caller does not await result.

preconditions: All required services are initialized and importable
postconditions: Workflows produce side effects (DB writes, external calls, socket emissions) or return domain objects
Fire-and-forget workflows may fail silently—caller does not observe the error

nodes.label: Upload (R2, 3-retry exp backoff)
nodes.description: Upload files to Cloudflare R2 with 3 attempts (500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms exponential backoff). Returns { path, error } tuple—caller must check error field.

nodes.label: Thumbnail Generation
nodes.description: Generate 400×400 thumbnail: sharp for images (WebP quality 80), ffmpeg for videos (1s screenshot, 400px width). Upload result to R2 via storage.service.

nodes.label: Dynamic Watermarking
nodes.description: On-the-fly watermark images with @viewer.username via sharp composite (white text, 25% opacity, tiled). Upload to temp/ path with 5-min cache. Falls back to original unwatermarked on any error.

nodes.label: Scheduled Publish
nodes.description: Check content schedule on page load/feed fetch. If publishDate ≤ now, update status from 'scheduled' to 'published'. No cron job—only evaluated on access.

nodes.label: Content Deletion
nodes.description: Delete content: collect all R2 file paths from files[] JSONB, delete each via storage.service.deleteFromPrivate, then delete DB record. R2 delete failures do not block DB delete (orphaned files possible).

nodes.label: Crypto Verify (11-step)
nodes.description: Full on-chain verification: dedup hash, format check, wallet fetch, sandbox bypass (0x0000), network select, eth_getTransactionReceipt, receipt status, contract match, topics[2] parse, data field decode, amount comparison (1¢ tolerance), platform fee calc, DB insert.

nodes.label: Fee Calculation (12.5%)
nodes.description: Calculate platform fee: DEFAULT_COMMISSION_RATE (12.5%) from constants.ts, with Enclave override (10%, not yet implemented) and per-creator commission_rate override (not yet implemented).

nodes.label: Payout Request
nodes.description: Process payout: verify wallet config, validate amount, recalculate available balance from Cleared transactions, verify amount ≤ available, call processDebitCardOffRamp (mocked → returns fake tr_offramp_<random>).

nodes.label: Referral Bonus
nodes.description: Award referral bonus on signup: match email to Enclave application, grant Enclave benefits, or track referral code. Milestone check: ≥$750 earnings, within 30-day window, $25 speed bonus if within 14 days.

nodes.label: Send Message
nodes.description: Create message in DB, emit new_message Socket.IO event to conversation room, generate signed URLs for content attachments.

nodes.label: Mass Message
nodes.description: Creator broadcast: fetch all active subscribers, filter by min tier, personalize {{username}} template, call sendDirectMessage per subscriber sequentially. Returns count of successful sends.

nodes.label: Ticket to DM Sync
nodes.description: Admin replies to ticket → support.service appends to ticket + calls MessageService.sendDirectMessage via dynamic require. User reply → message.service detects admin receiver → calls supportService.appendUserMessageToActiveTicket → ticket status changes Pending→Open.

nodes.label: Notification Broadcast
nodes.description: Batch-create notifications for active subscribers: fetch subscriptions, filter active, fetch preferences, for each enabled subscriber build and execute createNotification promise. Fire-and-forget with .catch().

nodes.label: Login
nodes.description: Authenticate user via Supabase Auth signInWithPassword, fetch profile via findUserById, reshape via reshapeUserForApp, return { user, token }.

nodes.label: Signup + Orphan Cleanup
nodes.description: Create Supabase Auth user, create profile row, handle referral code. On profile failure: delete auth user via admin.deleteUser. If delete fails: permanent orphan (auth user exists without profile).

nodes.label: Password Reset
nodes.description: Accept forgot-password request, call supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail, always return success (enumeration prevention). User clicks email link, submits new password, update via admin.updateUserById.

nodes.label: Event Log
nodes.description: Log analytics event: skip if viewer is admin/self, insert row into analytics_events. If post_view: call increment_content_view_count RPC. RPC failure is silently logged—event still recorded.

nodes.label: Content View Increment
nodes.description: Atomic increment of content.stats.views via supabase.rpc('increment_content_view_count', { content_id_to_update }). Called after successful post_view event logging.

nodes.label: Summary Aggregation
nodes.description: Monthly analytics aggregation: count events grouped by creator/type for monthly_analytics_summary table. Called from admin dashboard and creator analytics.

nodes.label: Dashboard Stats
nodes.description: Admin dashboard: 5 parallel queries (countAllUsers, countActiveCreators, sumPlatformFeeForPeriod(30), countOpenTickets, getNewUsersOverTime(6)). No caching—runs 5 queries per page load.

nodes.label: Content Moderation
nodes.description: Moderation pipeline: user reports content → report created → if count ≥ 3 auto-flag → admin views flagged content (enriched with reportCount + creator) → admin approves (published, reports auto-dismissed) or removes (status: removed).

nodes.label: Verification Doc Access
nodes.description: Admin requests verification docs: check verification_data JSONB for idFilePath + selfieFilePath, call StorageService.getPrivateSignedUrl(filePath, 60), return 60-second signed URLs containing PII (government ID, selfie).

validationRules: Upload caller must check error field—service does not throw on upload failure
Fire-and-forget workflows must never throw unhandled rejections
Watermarking must never block content viewing—always falls back to original
businessRules: Only R2 upload implements retry logic (3 attempts, exp backoff)
No workflow uses a queue/broker—all execute synchronously or as unawaited promises
Content creation is the only workflow with storage rollback on failure
reshapeUserForApp is the most-called internal function (23 call sites)
securityConsiderations: Watermark fallback degrades to unwatermarked original—bypasses content protection
Orphan cleanup failure creates permanent auth user without profile
Fire-and-forget notifications may fail silently—no audit trail
performanceConsiderations: MassMsg iterates subscribers sequentially—O(n) synchronous calls
CryptoVerify makes external RPC call (2-10 seconds latency)
DashboardStats runs 5 parallel DB queries per page load

annotations.text: Only workflow with retry logic—3 attempts, exponential backoff (500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms)
Fire-and-forget via .catch()—caller does not await. Failures silently logged.
0x0000 sandbox bypass skips all on-chain checks—any authenticated user can create verified transactions
Off-ramp is MOCKED—returns fake transaction ID. No real payout mechanism.
